key_insight: LeanSide lets students write natural-language proofs while a verified Lean backend checks each step and translates feedback back into human-friendly language.
engineering_relevance: It shows how formal verification can be wrapped in an educational co-reasoning interface to improve trust, guidance, and usability for theorem-proving systems.
method: Built a co-reasoning loop that auto-formalizes student proof text into Lean.
Uses a verified backend to check reasoning and informally explain errors or next-step feedback.
Studied the system through classroom deployment with undergraduate mathematics students.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports user studies from classroom deployment analyzing which system properties helped students progress and which caused them to get stuck.
watch_item: A key implementation concern is that the auto-formalization/feedback pipeline may still misalign with student intent, causing users to stall despite verification.
paper_title: LeanSide: A Formally Verified Co-Reasoning System for Natural-language Proofs
